area_overview: Procedural T-SQL and stored procedures: BEGIN/END, IF, variables, SET/SELECT assignment, CREATE/ALTER PROCEDURE, parameters, OUTPUT parameters, rowversion/return patterns.
key_ideas: BEGIN/END groups multiple statements into one block for IF/procedure bodies.
Stored procedures encapsulate reusable T-SQL with parameters and result sets.
Parameters can be input or OUTPUT; OUTPUT must be marked in both procedure definition and call site.
DECLARE creates variables; SET and SELECT can assign values, with different behavior when a query returns multiple rows.
IF/ELSE drives procedural branching; IF EXISTS is often used for existence checks.
rowversion is a binary concurrency token, not a date/time value.
Procedures can communicate results through SELECT result sets, OUTPUT parameters, return codes, and rows affected.
When returning newly changed values, SQL Server's OUTPUT clause and stored procedure OUTPUT parameters solve different problems.
